1) the predictive power of behavioral sequences is much stronger than the predictive power of the pre survey; and 2) the predictive power is stronger for the trustor's behavior than the trustee's behavior, and the predictive power increases with the length of the sequence.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether a human agent interaction (e.g. HAI) agent can accurately model its human teammates and predict their trust behaviors.
the problem of predicting future trust behavior of a human agent based on limited information.
the question of how to generate accurate expectations of a human's behavior based only on observations of their trust related actions, and we demonstrate a method for achieving this.

a Markovian method for predicting trust behavior in human agent interaction is a method that can be used to predict the future behavior of a human agent based on the past behavior of the agent and the current situation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the initial trust related personality traits are not a good indicator of future trust behavior, they can be used in conjunction with behavioral sequences to improve prediction accuracy.
, although the pre survey data is not a good predictor for trust behavior during the interaction, it can be used as a starting point to predict future behavior, which is more important for the agent.

, given a sequence of past trust behaviors by a human teammate, a robot agent can generate accurate predictions of its future behavior.
an agent can generate expectations about its teammates' trust behaviors by analyzing sequences of prior behavior, even if it does not know their individual characteristics.
